heuristics.statement: For the fixed walk f(u) = LE256(BLAKE3_r7(0^32 || LE256(u))) XOR PD (seven rounds is the full BLAKE3 round count), the success probability of the frozen algorithm over its uniform offset rho is at least the random-function lower bound of proof Section P (exact value above 0.41393), and in particular at least 0.39.
heuristics.scope: Transfers the random-function theorem of proof Section P to the fixed target. The algorithm is generic and uses only that answers to fresh queries along the lane-serialized search are uniform and independent of the history.
heuristics.extrapolation: Experiments blake3-r7-slice-first-collision-w20-v1 and -w24-v1 test the first-duplicate mechanism on 512 independent 20- and 24-bit slices of the fixed target, with the same kernel, consecutive starts and lane serialization as the search; under the model the probability of a returned pair is exactly 0.448648 and 0.237789 (99 percent intervals 94-136 and 43-79 of 256, fixed before execution; family-wise false-alarm rate about 1.3 percent; power limited to shifts of roughly 0.07-0.08). Extrapolation from these widths to the 2^128-query full-width regime rests on the design and public analysis of full BLAKE3, not on measurement.
heuristics.limitations: Plausible, not established. The experiments cannot test full-width distinguished-point and key events, the full function rather than its slices, or properties appearing only at full scale. The random-function event cover has been reviewed by its authors only. The 14-bit implementation diagnostic is not used as probability evidence.

heuristics.statement: The cost model's 256-bit word RAM is realized as a load/store machine with a fixed file of 32 registers of 256 bits (the AVX-512 vector register count). Every access to any other word is a separately charged load or store: the kernel uses explicit spill code (17,433 loads and 13,476 stores per batch) and control code is charged as load-op-store. The algorithm is the fixed program image of proof Section 3.2 (331,392 bytes), counted in memory; instruction fetch is not a primitive operation. COMP computes the complete one-block root compression of M(a) for one compression unit plus its operand load, result store and 64 word operations for block assembly.
heuristics.scope: Accounting convention for proof Sections 3, M and L. The only free choice affecting time is the register count; the deterministic event bounds and hash-evaluation counts do not depend on it.
heuristics.extrapolation: The kernel listing, its static correctness proof, the image round trip and the handler closed forms are asserted by the declared experiment. Sensitivity: 16 registers give 2^126.05171, three registers 2^127.16838, and charging instruction fetch at one load per 32 bytes of kernel code gives 2^126.08934; instruction encoding affects memory only.
heuristics.limitations: The cost model fixes no register count; 32 is this entry's declaration, motivated by existing 256-bit SIMD hardware. The Python generator that produces the image is provenance tooling and is not part of the attack.

heuristics.statement: The generated kernel (46,111 gates scheduled as a 77,020-instruction load/store listing) computes the planes of f(u) from the planes of u for every 256-bit input u.
heuristics.scope: Correctness of the bitsliced main-loop evaluation, on which the success-probability argument depends. Recovery and the final check use the scalar compression and verify the returned pair explicitly.
heuristics.extrapolation: The declared experiment checks every gate-construction rule exhaustively on all operand classes (6,191 cases over all input assignments) and proves statically that the load/store listing (with its spill code) computes the gate DAG for every input. The word-level composition follows the BLAKE3 specification line for line and is cross-checked by sampled full-digest agreement with scalar BLAKE3, including every organizer-verified slice pair.
heuristics.limitations: The composition step (that build_listing applies the BLAKE3 operations in specification order) is established by inspection and sampling, not by a mechanical equivalence proof.

restrictions: Ordinary collision construction for the complete seven-round BLAKE3 hash (blake3-r7-prefix-v1) on 64-byte messages 0^32 || LE256(u); no complete collision is exhibited and the attack is not executed at full scale.

time_log2 and memory_log2_bytes are worst-case bounds derived from the fixed program image on a 32-register load/store machine with every memory access charged; with 16 registers the time bound would be 126.05171 and with three registers 127.16838. This entry does not claim to improve on the published round-7 entry a2e94df7.

success_probability rests on the random-function theorem of proof Section P (reviewed by its authors only) and the declared heuristic H1, supported by exact-law slice experiments at widths 20 and 24; the 14-bit machine diagnostic is implementation evidence only.
